name: Nosferatu: Applied Disciplines, Traits, and Tactics

text.content:
With the Storyteller's permission, a Nosferatu player may describe her deformity using one of these evocative adjectives instead of a generic descriptor such as Bestial or Repugnant. They function identically to any other descriptive Trait (comparable to Brawny or Impatient) and should be incorporated into roleplaying, not just written on a card.

Optional Nosferatu Traits: Blighted, Blubbery, Charred, Dreadful, Engorged, Flaccid, Mangy, Nauseating, Oozing, Petrified, Putrefied, Pustulent, Reptilian, Repulsive, Rubbery, Scabrous, Scarred, Skanky, Withered.

pages.name: Unusual Applications of the Clan Disciplines

text.content:
Elder Nosferatu put their three clan Disciplines to uses far beyond their obvious combat or stealth applications. These are roleplaying suggestions for Narrators and players rather than new mechanics; use the existing power write-ups for the actual challenge resolution.

Animalism

  • Scouts: With Feral Whispers, any alley cat, sewer rat, or street dog can be sent to scout a corner, sneak into a building, or shadow a suspicious character, often more effectively than an Obfuscate-based spy.
  • Guard Animals: Training a lookout is far simpler through Animalism than through the Animal Ken Ability; even a lowly cat or rat can watch a Nosferatu's back.
  • Diversions: Beckoning need not summon an attacking swarm. A flock of pigeons fluttering around pursuers, or a single dog on a walk, can create a distraction a horde of sewer rats cannot.
  • Mental Manipulation: Quell the Beast can convince a mortal witness that a skulking monster isn't such a threat after all, buying time to bind, gag, or otherwise deal with him; it also doubles as a feeding technique (see below).
  • Bestial Revelry: Some bestial Nosferatu prefer Subsume the Spirit to Mask of a Thousand Faces, freely roaming the surface world as a rabid dog or feral cat; Auspex does not detect this possession.
  • Animal Spies: A vampire with Heightened Senses may notice a Nosferatu's Unseen Presence but rarely thinks twice about the alley cat that just wandered in. This oblivious attitude is the backbone of many Nosferatu information networks.

Obfuscate

  • Video and Audio Surveillance: Selling secrets doesn't require mastery of Obfuscate. A spy needs only to stay silent and stay still with a camera or microphone (Cloak of Shadows); another brood member using Cloak the Gathering can rendezvous with him afterward.
  • Social Chaos: Mask of a Thousand Faces can impersonate a primogen, a prince, or a mortal celebrity, sowing chaos in local Camarilla politics if a Nosferatu brood isn't shown proper respect.
  • Urban Renewal: Some Nosferatu use social chaos on kine neighborhoods directly, encouraging condemnations and demolitions, atrocities blamed on a "local policeman," or gang turmoil to turn a neighborhood into an accessible aboveground haven over time.
  • Falsified Blackmail: Mask of a Thousand Faces plus a camera can manufacture incriminating photographs of politicians, celebrities, or ordinary marks; the picture doesn't even need to be real to be worth a fortune.

Potence

  • Construction: Expanding a city's sewer domain often means using Potence to tunnel through rock, move rubble, or collapse an unstable passage the ghouls can't manage alone.
  • Destruction: A common last-ditch defense collapses chosen hallways to block an invading force; the same strength can bring down an aboveground building on an unwary enemy lured inside.
  • Sculpture: Nosferatu art favors massive stone and metal pieces; Potence lets a sculptor chip marble or bend iron, making Performance a surprisingly useful Ability for the clan.
  • Wrestling: Various legendary Nosferatu combine Potence with wrestling styles, from Greco-Roman grappling to Mexican lucha libre, against mortal and supernatural opponents alike.
  • Hurling Things: Why throw a punch when you can throw a sewer lid, a gate, or a car? See Potent Combat, below, for the improvised-weapon rules this enables.

A Nosferatu with Potence is never without a weapon when there's an iron gate, a sewer lid, or a parked car nearby. In live-action play, such feats of strength should be as difficult as they are ridiculous to pull off, and a Narrator should feel free to keep a few prop cards on hand specifically for improvised weapons rather than making a player mime hoisting a pickup truck overhead.

MET Rule: Any improvised weapon of this sort carries the Negative Trait Unwieldy x3, making it harder to hit a target with, though it does not reduce the damage it inflicts. Improvised weapon damage is calculated by taking the item's listed damage dice (from the tabletop system) and dividing by two for Trait purposes, at Storyteller discretion.

Example Improvised Weapons (Feat of Strength difficulty / approximate damage):

  • Sewer Lid: difficulty 5, roughly 4 health levels of damage.
  • Thrown Gate: difficulty 7, roughly 4 health levels of damage.
  • Motorcycle: difficulty 9, roughly 4-5 health levels of damage.
  • Compact Car: difficulty 11, roughly 5 health levels of damage.

Humans flee from hideous creatures, so stalking prey aboveground is harder for Nosferatu than for clans with Dominate or Presence. Obfuscate helps, but not every Sewer Rat has it, and neonates especially must improvise. These are established feeding tactics used across the clan.

  • Ghouled Slaves: Blood-addicted ghouls sometimes lure prey to a secluded place as a gift to their masters, sparing the vampire the need to stalk anyone at all.
  • Blood Dolls: Capture a human, ghoul him, addict him to your vitae, and nurture the blood bond; he'll allow regular feeding of his own accord, though Nosferatu blood dolls tend to become physically warped and degenerate over time.
  • Quell the Beast: This Animalism power works on any sentient creature, including mortals. Repeated use on the same alley or street corner lulls victims into a pacified, addictive trance; they keep returning with hazy memories of the Kiss.
  • Sandmen: Sneaking into a victim's home at night to feed while he sleeps; the old folklore about needing an invitation is convenient misinformation. Plan an escape route carefully, since not every home has a sewer grate nearby.
  • Thugs: Using Potence to knock a victim out with a single blow, then carrying him off to feed at leisure; failed Sandmen often fall back on simply smashing down a door.
  • Bogeymen: Feeding on children, playing on the legends of monsters that lurk for misbehaving kids; frightened parents are quick to disbelieve a child's description of his attacker.
  • The Internet: Gathering a target's official records and the secrets he lets slip in chat rooms and forums to identify an ideal victim for thralldom, the Embrace, or an occasional feeding, all without ever showing your face.
  • Pack Tactics: Hunting as a coterie or brood, flushing prey from cover and tracking it through the streets as a team, whether operating within Camarilla structure or running loose as part of a Sabbat pack.
